tests.name: test_small_synthetic_z_mode_builds_only_one_labeled_proxy
tests.claim: One hand-written manifest record survives build_datasets labeled and alone, for both the JAM and NNPDF small-closure config/datasets pairs.
tests.actual: built[0].name/.source/.component/.n_data exactly equal the literal name/classification/observable_contract/row-count the test wrote into the manifest a few lines earlier; len(built)==1; bilinear_contributions is nonempty; TEST_MODE_SYNTHETIC_Z is a member of TEST_MODES (a static config.py fact unrelated to the build). Does not assert built[0].mean or .cov at all. The JAM and NNPDF parametrized cases execute byte-identical build_datasets/build_drell_yan code (diffed directly), so they exercise one mechanism twice, not two implementations.
tests.how: writes a manifest.json literal into tmp_path, monkeypatches config.truth_dir to return that directory, calls build_datasets(q_key='mc', include_synthetic_z=True, all other include_* False), asserts fields on built[0] against the literals written above
tests.bar: exact `==` on strings/int, `in` membership on a tuple, truthiness on a tuple -- no float tolerance anywhere in this file
tests.catches: a wiring bug that drops, empties, or misroutes a manifest field into the wrong Dataset/DatasetMetadata attribute, or an emptied DY_CHANNELS x field-map cross product (bilinear_contributions would be empty). Does NOT catch: (1) a build that corrupts or drops mean/cov -- measured directly, see measurements; (2) a name<->label field mixup in build_drell_yan's rec.get('name', rec['label']) -- both fixture fields are the identical literal string 'synthetic_z_plumbing'.

tests.name: test_small_synthetic_z_rejects_missing_or_unclassified_manifest
tests.claim: Both build_datasets synthetic_z guard clauses raise their documented text.
tests.actual: A manifest with zero synthetic_z records raises ValueError matching 'exactly one'. A manifest with one record classified 'physics' (not 'synthetic_proxy') raises ValueError matching 'synthetic_proxy'. Only the JAM config/datasets pair is exercised; not parametrized over NNPDF.
tests.how: writes two different malformed manifest.json literals in sequence inside one test body, wraps each build_datasets call in pytest.raises(ValueError, match=<substring>)
tests.bar: pytest.raises exception type + literal message substring match -- structural, no numeric content
tests.catches: either guard clause being deleted or its exception type/message changed past the matched substring. Does NOT catch: the 'exactly one' guard weakening to 'at least one' (2+ records is never tried, only 0 and 1); any regression in closure_NNPDF_truth_small's identical guard clauses (zero coverage, JAM-only test).

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 as DOCUMENTATION-ONLY (no strengthening, and none was proposed: this weakness's own proposed_fix concluded no code change was required). VERIFIED present in the file this pass -- tests/test_small_synthetic_z.py:29-38 and :49 record that build_datasets/build_drell_yan and the DY config constants are identical between the two packages, so the parametrization is a JAM/NNPDF drift guard rather than two independent cases. Recorded here because the JSON was left unannotated when the documentation landed; a reader of the report alone would have counted this as outstanding work. The underlying limitation is unchanged and is stated in the file. tests/test_small_synthetic_z.py:81-87 parametrizes over (jam_config, jam_datasets) and (nnpdf_config, nnpdf_datasets); `diff closure_JAM_truth_small/datasets.py closure_NNPDF_truth_small/datasets.py` shows exactly 2 hunks in the whole file -- one docstring cross-reference line, one unrelated kwarg-line reorder inside build_pseudoitd -- and build_datasets/build_drell_yan are untouched; the DY-relevant config.py constants (DY_ORDER, DY_ALPHA_EM, DY_ALPHA_S, DY_NF, DY_CHANNELS, DY_FIT_NORMALIZATION, dy_field_maps, DY_PARTON_BASIS_PROTON/DEUTERON) are identical in value between the two config.py files.

Now disclosed in both the module and per-test docstring, so no longer a silent gap, but the underlying redundancy is unchanged.

missing.rationale: RESOLVED 2026-08-14 by test_generation_time_synthetic_z_layout_is_what_the_manifest_reader_consumes -- without running the generator (owner instruction, no closure pipeline runs). It takes the real synthetic_z_layout() record, applies _public and the two keys generate_member adds at generate.py:578-580, and drives it through the reader; a key the generator stopped emitting or one the reader started requiring now fails here. Oracle A3 between the generation-time build_drell_yan(rec, None, fields, None) call at generate.py:566 and the fitting-time build_datasets manifest route: measured 360 bilinear contributions whose (field_A, field_B) pairs match as an ordered sequence and whose weights are array-equal. Acceptance: mut_sz_layout_renames_a_key (observable_contract renamed in synthetic_z_layout, applied to both copies so the identity test stays out of it) makes it fail; 1 failed / 7 passed. generate.py's synthetic_z_layout() (line 217, JAM/NNPDF-identical) is the real production source of the manifest record this test hand-writes, and generate_member's synthetic_z block (generate.py:469-493) folds it through the same build_drell_yan and through dy_central, then writes it into manifest.json under the same 'synthetic_z' key this test's reader consumes.
